request.amount_ada: 500,000,000 ada net change limit; no treasury withdrawal requested
request.deadline: Close of Epoch 713, stated as on or about July 3, 2027
deliverables: Set a fixed cap on total ada removed from the Treasury through Treasury Withdrawals during the period.
Apply the limit from the start of Epoch 613 through the close of Epoch 713.
Count Treasury Withdrawals already debited during the period toward the limit.
Supersede any prior Net Change Limit for the same period.
Record DRep agreement if Yes votes exceed 50% of active voting stake.
request.what: Info action to agree a new Net Change Limit for Cardano Treasury withdrawals during Epochs 613-713.

claims.claim: The proposal sets a new Cardano Treasury Net Change Limit of 500,000,000 ada for Epochs 613-713.
The proposed limit caps only Treasury Withdrawals debited from the Cardano Treasury and recorded on the Cardano ledger during the period.
Treasury inflows, including reserve and protocol allocations, transaction-fee allocations, refunds, and returned Treasury-funded amounts, do not count toward or increase the proposed limit.
Treasury Withdrawals already debited during the period beginning at Epoch 613 count toward the 500,000,000 ada cumulative limit.
The proposal states that it has no direct on-chain effect and does not authorize any Treasury Withdrawal.
The proposal states that it supersedes any prior Net Change Limit for the same Epochs 613-713 period, including the existing 350,000,000 ada limit.
The proposer asserts that practical room under the existing 350,000,000 ada limit is becoming constrained.
The proposer asserts that a 500,000,000 ada limit preserves DRep ability to consider credible Treasury Withdrawals on their merits while retaining a clear fixed fiscal guardrail.
The proposal says it is drafted to comply with the enacted Cardano Constitution version 2.4 and Appendix I Guardrails, and provides an IPFS reference to that Constitution.

summary: The anchor document is an Info action proposing a higher Treasury net-change cap, not a direct withdrawal, with detailed accounting rules but limited evidence for why the higher cap is needed.
